## 2026-10-07 — Explicit application state machines (proposal)

**Observed gap.** Can already expresses business lifecycles through enum fields, guarded scenarios and ordered `set` effects. ExpenseFlow owns its initial state at `Expense.status`, but source-state checks, target assignments and locks live in separate declarations ([example](../../examples/ExpenseFlow.can)). The inspected compiler syntax has no dedicated application machine/transition construct. Existing state and work runtime code supplies mutation admission, provisional state, fenced commits, history, receipts, outbox and scheduling; this inspection does not establish complete application execution.

**Proposed direction.** Explore an opt-in lifecycle on a stored model field, with transition edges owned by existing canonical scenarios or verified trusted handlers. Derive graph/tooling metadata from those declarations and enforce the lifecycle through the existing compiler and state authority. Keep operation parameters, `by`, business guards, inline examples, record versions and durable effects with their current owners. A transition would have an explicit position within `do`: source validation and state change occur there against ordered provisional state, and later failure rolls back the whole operation. Ordinary CRUD, `set`, hooks and other writers must not bypass an opted-in lifecycle; creation and migrations require their own explicit contracts. This is a design sketch, not accepted grammar or an implemented effect.

**Alternatives and advice.** Better enum/scenario conventions plus graph analysis preserve current simplicity, but cannot promise a complete graph for arbitrary conditions and assignments. A reusable named machine type provides central graph reuse, but must integrate existing operation identity, schemas and authority without copying them. Three independently worded equivalent JEV choice requests select the model-bound direction with probabilities **0.65/0.47/0.43** and confidence **0.53/0.29/0.24**. Existing idioms retain **0.21/0.38/0.28** probability and deferral **0.11/0.03/0.23**. The responses supply no rationale; wording review found no fact reversal, and the variation remains unresolved uncertainty rather than a robust architectural verdict. [Requests, responses and assessment](../design/jev/state-machines-20261007/assessment.json) preserve the evidence. Advice supports investigation only.

**Remaining design work.** Decide field opt-in and graph reuse, typed source/target sets, branch/repeated-transition semantics, creation/fixture/import/migration rules, error ordering, graph evolution and every mutation path. Preserve edge-to-operation/site associations: identical source/target pairs can have different permissions and inputs. Provisional field reads through aliases, queries and nested calls must agree; runtime protected-field enforcement, hook transition eligibility and per-transition versus final-state history need explicit contracts. A failed transition rolls back earlier staged effects too; nothing is externally delivered before commit. Replayed requests, competing decisions and late timers/completions need concrete witnesses, including leaving and reentering the same state; a state-name check alone does not establish occurrence freshness. Terminal lifecycle state does not automatically freeze other fields or alter deletion/retention. UI availability must remain advisory, permission-filtered and rechecked by the server. Nested/parallel/history states, automatic entry/exit effects, eventless cascades and standalone in-memory machine reuse remain open scope, not assumed unnecessary. [SCXML](https://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/) and [Stately transitions](https://stately.ai/docs/transitions) provide reference semantics, not selected dependencies.

**Verification and scope.** Source/specification inspection and request/response JSON checks only. No compiler/runtime implementation, grammar adoption, app migration or behavioral test execution. A fair next design comparison needs complete before/after witnesses for simple approval and an existing durable workflow, with their permissions, failure outcomes and authoring costs retained. No merge or living-filetree checkpoint advance.

## 2026-10-08 — Initial patch-first interpretation of agent repair

**Status:** The patch-first interface below was an interpretation of the user's request and is superseded by the keyword-help clarification in the following decision. Its consultation remains recorded as design evidence for optional future patches.

**Earlier interpretation:** An AI coding agent new to Can should need only a tiny Given/When/Then orientation. It may write plausible but invalid `.can`, including invented declaration shapes; the development error should guide it toward concrete canonical source, preferably with an exact candidate patch at the error location. Jev would judge the closest intended interpretation among supplied valid edits or canonical construct families. Unknown syntax still fails compilation; the agent must choose and recheck source before execution.

**Superseded proposal:** The compiler would derive bounded edit candidates from expected grammar, canonical constructs and resolved declarations, check each edit against the pinned source revision, and expose the leading patch in a compact development error backed by a hash-guarded code action. Jev would rank supplied, checked candidates with a none/unclear option, while the compiler alone determined validity. A text-generating candidate fallback was an unaccepted later option. The clarified keyword-help design follows below.

**Rationale and uncertainty:** TypeSafe describes Jev as making typed decisions over supplied alternatives rather than generating source text, so a candidate producer and deterministic validator are necessary for a patch in an error. Three equivalent, independently worded [Jev consultations](../design/jev/can-dev-repair-20261008/assessment.md) favored compiler-derived candidates plus Jev ranking (probabilities 0.63, 0.97 and 0.87; confidence 0.51, 0.96 and 0.83). This is advice on a synthetic design choice, not evidence of real agent completion or token savings. Current diagnostics, parser recovery and edit transport provide foundations, but no syntax-repair candidate provider or `can dev` session exists. Candidate coverage, wrong-intent rate and the value of a generative fallback require measured unfamiliar-agent tasks.

## 2026-10-08 — Give an unfamiliar agent the nearest real Can construct

**Accepted user clarification:** For an unknown or invented `.can` word, Jev should identify the closest working keyword or construct when one fits. The development error returns that construct's canonical signature, a short description and a link to its reference, with plausible alternatives and uncertainty. This is the primary teaching loop for agents given only minimal Given/When/Then rules. A full code patch is optional for a mechanical mapping; the agent can write the source using the help and check again.

**Proposed mechanism, not an existing API:** The compiler supplies a finite set of context-eligible construct IDs using its grammar and completion facts. Jev uses a Choice question over those IDs plus none/unclear; the development server joins the ranked ID to version-pinned Can-owned help metadata. The metadata, rather than Jev, supplies the signature, meaning, minimal example and documentation link. Keep the top card compact in the error, with alternatives addressable by ID. A suggested construct is not a compiled replacement or an authority decision. [The living dev-server design](../design/can-dev-server.md) holds the example and proposed response flow.

**Rationale and open evidence:** The current LSP completion already selects source words by syntactic position, while its keyword entries have no signature, description or link. `can explain` documents error codes, not individual constructs. A shared, versioned help index and Jev matcher remain to be built. The three prior Jev consultations compared patch-first alternatives and do not evaluate this clarified keyword-first interface. Measure construct ranking accuracy, agent completion, wrong-intent choices and total tokens against deterministic position-aware help before claiming a benefit from Jev.


## 2026-10-09 — Prepare the Can dev contracts before implementation planning

**Status:** [The pre-planning checklist](../design/can-dev-server.md#before-an-implementation-plan) is proposed work to make a later implementation plan evidence-based; it does not accept tool names, transport, first runtime profile or delivery stages. The proposed [three unfamiliar-agent app tasks](../design/can-dev-agent-tasks.md) now give copy-ready prompts and observable checks for office supplies, staff shifts and expense review, with only the tiny Given/When/Then introduction shown to the agent. They remain a benchmark draft until their runtime profile and scoring boundaries are qualified. The checklist also asks for the construct-help source and error contract, a Jev ranking comparison, one real preview/example feasibility check, session and failure-evidence boundaries, and first-slice acceptance criteria. The current local Miniflare helper is dispatch-only and the CLI test path reports zero executed rows, so the planned preview and example loop cannot yet be treated as existing. Record choices and uncertainty after those checks, then derive implementation tasks from the selected contracts.

**First-draft observation, not an accepted repair design:** [Six raw unfamiliar-agent drafts and annotations](../design/evaluation/can-dev-novice-20261009/findings.md) were collected with only the tiny introduction and one task prompt. All six were rejected by the existing local debug compiler; four first failed at top-level app structure and two at indentation. Actual guessed forms include prose `Given`/`When`/`Then` headers, `rule`, `permit`, `atomic`, invented UI words and non-executable example prose. Several require none/unclear or structural guidance because no single keyword preserves their meaning. This sample does not measure iterative completion or Jev value; keep the keyword-help contract and first-slice scope open until those comparisons are run.

**Proposed construct-help reference, not a shipped endpoint:** [The anchored Can v1 catalog](CONSTRUCT-HELP.md) records 278 distinct help IDs with signatures, meanings, contextual examples, availability and stable self-links. Its 70 UI cards cover the 68 authored UI words, with separate calendar and tabs contexts; its 36 callable builtin cards match the Values catalog's authored builtin IDs and signatures. Grammar/design and owning UI/Values catalogs retain language and runtime authority; this document is the single authored help text at the design stage. A future compiler-owned structured projection must replace or generate it, not form a second independent copy. The existing local debug compiler reported no diagnostics for 202 full-looking examples; other fragments and runtime behavior were not qualified. Current completion omits some implemented forms, historical grammar prototype caveats conflict with Rust branches, and provider, resource and corpus availability still need selected-profile checks before any card is called working. Three balanced [Jev consultations and their disagreement](../design/jev/can-dev-help-20261009/assessment.md) informed ownership but did not settle serialization or prove agent benefit.

**Proposed Jev construct-routing trial, not implemented:** [The ranking contract](../design/can-dev-jev-ranking.md) returns exact grammar/help matches deterministically and asks Jev only when two to eight verified, profile-eligible meanings remain at a reliable diagnostic location. One selected primary occurrence per check receives a bounded, redacted source/declaration packet and optional explicitly supplied task-intent sentence; full files, secrets and runtime values stay local. `none` and `unclear` remain distinct, and a numerical top-card gate is a trial display rule, never permission or proof of a valid edit. Incomplete/recovered context, incomplete candidate coverage, unsupported behavior and unresolved authority/effect choices abstain. A delayed, invalid or unavailable provider leaves compiler diagnostics and deterministic help intact, and an old-revision rank is discarded. Three balanced [Jev consultations](../design/jev/can-dev-ranking-20261009/assessment.md) favored ambiguity-only routing (0.97/0.58/0.83); evidence-scope advice split between bounded context and structured-only, so the selected packet minimizes source text. The current compiler has no structured expected-token/root-cause field, the ranking join is absent, and no corpus comparison establishes accuracy, latency or token savings.

**Construct-help comparison pilot, still unqualified:** [The frozen local baseline and protocol](../design/evaluation/can-dev-help-comparison-20261009/RESULTS.md) use the same three unfamiliar-agent tasks and six observed first drafts. All six first errors are structural (four `E1211`, two `E1103`), so the proposed router would not invoke Jev at those sites. Six deeper manually extracted construct probes have fixed candidate sets and gold intent before external ranking, but are not compiler-established eligible occurrences. The local debug binary checks all six drafts as invalid and fails compilation of the two reference apps on UI lowering; full task completion cannot be inferred from clean source checking or the current zero-row example CLI. External Jev and paired agent measurements await approval to transmit the exact project-derived probe packets and drafts after automatic approval review rejected that disclosure. Do not treat absent provider responses as zero wrong suggestions, zero tokens or zero latency.

**Selected compact dev error and exact-revision contract, not implemented:** [The versioned response](../design/can-dev-error-contract.md) shows one compiler diagnostic plus a small authoritative help card, counts and revision-bound cursors for other diagnostics. The machine reply retains full source-set SHA-256 over source paths and exact analyzed bytes; a session epoch pins selected app identity and that immutable capture together with compiler, catalog, help and profile inputs. Existing compiler per-file hashes and byte spans remain authoritative, with readable line/column derived from them. Structural uncertainty, `none`, `intent_unclear`, candidate-coverage gaps, incomplete/limited analysis and Jev failure are distinct states; no ranking can hide the diagnostic. Historical lookups stay historical or fail explicitly, and optional edits still require a current file hash. Compiler input-closure capture, unified help joins, dev references and serving build identity remain proposed; no full-project check is established by today's explicit-file CLI.

**Generation local runtime probe, observed but not an accepted first profile:** [The same-app feasibility check](../design/evaluation/can-dev-generation-local-20261009/README.md) selected the existing Generation source because it compiles with a page, D1-backed model and three authored `queue` rows. Its compiled anonymous page loaded in headless Chrome over an ephemeral loopback test bridge, and all three released browser resources served exact bundle bytes. A missing `DB` binding refused the page, but direct D1 inspection stalled; generated Worker `/auth/login` returned 501 `assembly-interim`, so signed-in state and mutations were not qualified. `can run` still returns a module URL without a listener. For this artifact `can test` failed at an unresolved `file:/` stdlib import before its hardcoded zero-row report, and direct suite loading exposed three callers but row setup failed on an unbound `job` fixture. Keep Generation as a feasibility witness only; first-profile acceptance requires the auth, artifact boot, fixture binding, row isolation and caller joins to run together. The result is based on existing local compiler/package outputs in a dirty worktree, not a fresh release build.

**Selected dev session, evidence and first control contract; unimplemented:** [The session/control design](../design/can-dev-session-control.md) chooses one owner-only live session per canonical checkout/worktree with a fixed app/profile, immutable source/input revisions, separate preview and per-row data scopes, and explicit stale-serving state. The compact failure occurrence wraps existing compiler, testkit, HTTP, invocation or delivery evidence; missing source mapping, trace, side-effect coverage and external-effect certainty remain visible rather than inferred. The first agent adapter is a JSON CLI over private local Unix IPC, with a separate authenticated loopback preview and a later development MCP adapter sharing the same session/evidence IDs. A selected example may be rerun in a fresh scope after its loader and actor path are qualified, but exact execution replay remains unavailable without a captured/restorable actor, clock, resource and provider capsule; ordinary receipt `replayed` is only a saved outcome. This choice favors existing JSON CLI reach, bounded output and one initial transport, while retaining MCP's native discovery as a reason to add it later. Three independently worded [Jev consultations](../design/jev/can-dev-session-control-20261009/assessment.md) favored JSON CLI (0.82/0.97/0.79) and isolated rerun (1.00/1.00/0.89), without rationale or agent-use measurement. Unix socket lifecycle, preview access cookie, closure capture, auth join, row execution, cross-owner correlation and replay qualification remain implementation/evaluation gaps; no runtime profile or whole first slice is accepted by this design choice.

## 2026-10-13 — BGI04 write leases, snapshots and journal recovery (accepted implementation)

One documented on-disk cooperative lease/journal protocol shared by both hosts. Canonical lock order is byte-wise ascending paths (release in reverse); write leases are exclusive `.can/gen/locks/<escaped>.write.lock` files, read leases are per-holder `<escaped>.read.<token>.lock` files; tokens are `v1-` plus 16 lowercase hex. One full-run journal per promotion under `.can/gen/runs/<run-id>/` stages the complete prior set (`old/`) plus replacements (`new/`) before an atomic `staged`→`committed` flip and atomic per-file apply; `.can/gen/previous/` retains exactly one wholesale prior group. Readers refuse while any `journal.json` is unresolved and compile immutable snapshots; recovery is idempotent in both directions, retains `conflict.json` plus staged/current material on unexpected bytes, and never overwrites participating work. Stopped-writer recovery requires explicit confirmation; leases never expire and are never stolen. Durability is qualified POSIX atomic rename with fsync (Linux/macOS); the protocol never claims filesystem CAS or uncooperative-writer protection. Rust: new `compiler/src/leases.rs` hook API (`acquire`/`release`, `stage_journal`/`mark_committed`/`apply_committed`/`commit_journal`/`recover_journal`, `snapshot_inputs`, `recover_stopped_writer`) plus a thin `source::snapshot_consumed_inputs` reader hook; `cli.rs` untouched for BGI-03 wiring. Node: new `packages/cloudflare/src/generation/{leases,journal}.ts` with colocated tests; lock bodies are byte-identical across hosts.

Remaining uncertainty: dispatcher wiring, fence integration with capture/accept, and multi-process hostile racing stay with BGI-03/BGI-05/BGI-12; Windows rename-replace semantics are best-effort and diagnose. Evidence: `cargo test --test bgi04_leases` 13/13, `--test bgi01_generation` 13/13, `--test bgi02_association` 14/14, compiled `node --test dist/generation/{leases,journal}.test.js` 12/12, existing `dist/generation/{records,association}.test.js` 10/10; zero tsc errors in generation files (2666 pre-existing errors elsewhere in the package); clippy clean on lib plus the three BGI targets.

## 2026-10-13 — `style` only names a reusable prompt; components carry their own style prompt

The human corrects how `$"prompts"` were being used in drafts. The `style` keyword can only name a prompt for reusability, so its sole form is the top-level Then definition `style Name $"prompt"` with no body. An inline `style` tag therefore makes no sense: no anonymous `style $"prompt"`, no `style Name` wrapper, child or leaf exists anywhere. Each component instead carries its own style directly — one `$"style prompt"` for a one-off or `$Name` for the reusable definition. A generated view is a component too: after its renderer prompt, its header may carry one second style suffix (`view Name(row:Model) $"renderer prompt" $"style prompt"` or `... $Name`) for its renderer root, and its only children remain its canonical controls, each with its own suffix. This supersedes the bounded generated-view root-style leaf and any ordinary style-wrapper meaning in the 2026-10-13 reusable-styles decision above; named-style reuse, saved-CSS sharing, per-use roots/hooks and the full-retry lifecycle are unchanged.

Applied to the drafts: the ten inline view-root `style` tags across CanApprove, CanBoard, CanDo, CanExpense, CanGallery, CanHire, CanInvoice, CanMember and CanPromptLab (nine anonymous, one named) moved onto their view headers, keeping every prompt text, style-unit identity and saved CSS association — only source-line associations moved to the header. The draft organizer now refuses any non-definition `style` statement and accepts the view-header second suffix, pinned by `draft/tools/test_organize.py`. Canonical wording in the build-generation requirements, choices, implementation contract/plan and JSON records, plus the then-ai-style Todo illustration (its two wrapper blocks became card suffixes), now states the same rule. Compiler/generator implementation remains BGI scope and unimplemented; no provider call or runtime claim.

0.56/0.45/0.72. Inspection confirmed `actions` currently means an operation list,

## 2026-10-14 — primary and secondary action priorities in Then

Accepted following explicit user direction: source declares action importance
with contextual `primary` and `secondary` suites. Primary controls are immediately
visible; secondary controls use the shared overflow menu. There is no public
`action_menu` spelling. Direct owners are page, card and row-bound view, with one
nonempty group of each priority per owner. Children reuse canonical form, edit,
delete and action bindings and keep their existing scope checks. A page Create
form needs no invented row; record controls still require their existing row.

The shared UI owns responsive heading placement, visible touch targets, menu
activation/dismissal, dialog focus and cancellation. Inputless ordinary actions
retain direct canonical submit; input forms open their existing prepared form,
and Archive/Delete always requires its canonical confirmation. Generated views
receive opaque primary/secondary bindings and arrange them unchanged. Forms,
preferences and dialog slots retain their existing submit/cancel placement. Other
container placements receive diagnostics until their specific ownership/layout
contract is accepted; this is not automatic action inference.

The [three host-scope consultations](../design/jev/action-priority-hosts-20261014/)
all selected page/card/view with canonical form plus record-control children, at
probabilities 0.89/0.97/0.99 and confidences 0.83/0.95/0.98. Source inspection
confirmed existing row-free form preparation and page-owned heading/children,
so page Create reuses established behavior. Broader overlay/collection placement
is separately proposed, not part of this implementation. The earlier naming
consultation remains historical evidence; the user's explicit choice governs.

Page heading composition preserves direct child boundaries through an optional
`PageDescriptor.renderParts` producer. Full and partial HTTP rendering select it
instead of the legacy joined-string renderer, so admission and authored children
still execute once. Legacy renderers keep their body intact. Cards already retain
separate child results; generated views retain their opaque bindings. Repeated
menu and confirmation identities encode the enclosing row occurrence using the
activation-safe hexadecimal alphabet. These are implementation details of the
existing page/control owners, not new source syntax or action invocation paths.

Real browser verification also requires native dialog lifecycle ownership:
settlement/removal calls `close()` before changing markup, while background reads
preserve an unrelated open dialog and its draft. A closed secondary popover keeps
its ancestor box renderable only while its owned modal is open; the popover stays
invisible and ignores pointer events, and the modal remains interactive. This
preserves canonical DOM/form ownership without parsing HTML or relocating forms.
The final native Can gate passed compile/build, seven examples and the complete
PromptStudio browser journey, and accepted the retained Sol 6.1/medium renderer.
The [existing execution view](../design/proposals/build-generation/implementation-plan.md#current-codex-integration-execution-view--2026-10-13)
records the single accepted report, eleven screenshots and scoped checks.

## 2026-10-14 — primary and secondary are labeled action primitives

Accepted user correction: each `primary` or `secondary` statement declares one
control, with required text/message caption and exactly one checked target. The
former bare priority suites and the claim that primary only means placement are
superseded. For example:

```can
primary "Approve" action=approve arguments={request=row}
secondary "Archive" action=Request.delete arguments={record=row}
```

Reuse the existing exclusive `action=`, `submit=true`, `opens=` and `target=`
bindings. Operation arguments retain their declared names/types and protected
record bindings; an action cannot infer authority from its visual placement.
Prepared operation controls reuse canonical admission, field grants, validation,
CSRF, version checks and delete confirmation. Complete inline, result-owning and
import/review forms remain canonical forms, with shared submit design. An authored
submit primitive suppresses the automatic submit instead of adding a duplicate.

Shared UI owns a fixed visible filled primary design and compact secondary menu
entries. No action-level style, tone, size or generated prompt overrides apply.
Cards place primary controls below their content and secondary controls in the
header; page controls use the toolbar. Multiple direct actions aggregate into one
action row and one menu while retaining canonical control identities and source
order. Nested owners and row/guard scopes retain their controls. Generated views
receive complete opaque `primary` and `secondary` bindings and reuse shared card
markup/classes for the surface, heading, metadata and footer. Scoped styles must
not enter canonical action or standard-submit markup.

The [three independent JEV requests](../design/jev/action-primitives-20261014/)
unanimously preferred reusing the existing checked binding family over limiting
primitives to operations or inventing another target language. This is design
advice, not verification of the implementation. Remaining uncertainty is actual
host-specific composition and draft workflow support; the BGI and DFE execution
views record the checks and unmet scope separately. All 50 draft sources were
migrated (539 primary, 162 secondary), preserving Given/When and complete form
workflows. Browser acceptance of every draft is not implied by this source change.


## 2026-10-14 — action owners determine shared placement

Accepted correction to the preceding action-primitive migration: priority syntax
is not meaningful under every visual component. In particular, a tooltip cannot
own a primary or secondary action. The previous migration preserved a tooltip
around CanLoyalty's redemption operation, and the compiler failed to reject that
placement. Generic aggregation at the authored position did not provide the
promised component-specific defaults.

The finite owner matrix is page, card, list/table record row, modal/drawer
`slot actions`, and the `details display=drawer` panel. Page actions occupy the
heading toolbar; card and panel primary actions occupy their footer and secondary
actions their heading menu; row actions occupy a trailing action area. Split
collections render the selected row actions in their detail panel heading/footer,
without evaluating unselected row suites. Canonical
form/edit permits only direct primary submit controls in its submit footer.
Fieldsets and other visual wrappers do not inherit action ownership. Active form
ownership excludes independent primitive operation/navigation/panel targets even
through a nested card. Existing read/result forms keep their original flow.

Tooltips, tabs, disclosures, heroes, joins, dropdowns and generic item slots are
not owners. Tooltip descendants cannot introduce priorities through cards or
expanded views. Other wrappers may contain a meaningful canonical owner or use
their existing ordinary checked trigger controls. Migrations preserve record aliases, permission
guards and result scope; they do not hoist controls to obtain admission.

This supersedes the preceding decision's direct generated-view priority bindings:
a generated view declares a canonical card in source and receives one complete
opaque `card` binding. The shared renderer owns its content and action placement;
the generated renderer cannot rearrange internal priority controls. This reuses
the existing card factory, checked targets and generated-binding carrier.

The [three independently worded JEV requests](../design/jev/action-owner-matrix-20261014/)
all advised explicit concrete owners over page/card-only wrapping or inherited
wrapper ownership (confidence 0.91, 0.95 and 0.96). There was no disagreement to
investigate. This is design advice, not evidence of browser acceptance. The
remaining uncertainty is integration of the complete draft corpus; the existing
DFE execution view retains its concrete compiler, composed-app and journey gaps.

The dedicated `tests/fixtures/action-gallery/ActionGallery.can` and
`tests/fixtures/action-forms/ActionForms.can` apps make these shared defaults
inspectable without an application's generated styling. The gallery covers page,
card, list/table row, modal, drawer, detail drawer and both split-collection
variants. The forms app covers direct primary submits and canonical cancellation;
it does not invent secondary actions inside forms. Each owns its native
validation entry point, Playwright journeys and desktop/mobile captures. Captures
are inspection evidence, not automatically approved visual references.

Browser integration exposed two shared-default defects. Complete sibling cards
inside a list row must stack in source order instead of sharing the upstream
list grid cell. Saved view mount registration must rescan the existing browser
client instead of stopping it: whole-client teardown clears selected detail
panels and can interrupt unrelated controls. View registration therefore changes
only the matching generated-view bindings. These are shared runtime fixes; the
inspection sources supply no special CSS or JavaScript workarounds.

## 2026-10-14 — rethink generated implementation persistence (superseded source-ID proposal)

At the user's request, reconsider the entire persistence mechanism through three independent architecture, identity/merge and lifecycle investigations followed by one coordinated corroboration round. The initial [persistence proposal](../design/proposals/build-generation/persistence-redesign.md) recommended retaining Git-tracked editable `can.generated/<id>/` groups and their existing record, replacing structural source matching with a tool-maintained ID on each owning prompt slot, and allocating new IDs from 128 random bits. Named uses share their definition; duplicate defining slots diagnose and can fork without AI. Preserve existing checked app/package ownership and qualify lookup by its defining root; add no module identity, global locator/lockfile or content-addressed object store. The suggested `gen=<id>` grammar was never accepted or implemented and is rejected by the user's subsequent clean-source requirement below.

Current source and one direct TypeScript check establish two concrete weaknesses: separate branches allocate the same next `u3`, and two explicitly bound duplicate inline nodes become ambiguous after only the enclosing source revision changes. The lifecycle review identifies direct compile's live/repeated reads, replacement journals without deletion semantics and text-encoded Git rollback as source-inspected risks; no concurrent-build corruption or crash recovery failure was reproduced. The recommendation requires one frozen consumed closure for every build entry point, exact add/replace/delete recovery and byte-safe assets. Missing inline output should diagnose uniformly, changing the present synthesized-empty-style exception. Compatibility, prompt drift and modified-since-generation remain separate; ordinary builds consume compatible saved edits with zero AI, while new contracts retain canonical authority and migration checks.

Three equivalent independently worded JEV Choice requests retain the same verified context and rotate balanced alternatives; [raw requests/results](../design/jev/persistence-redesign-20261014/1.json) and companion 2/3 records preserve uncertainty. `jev-1.13.0` returned 12 judgments using 8,510 tokens. All three preferred source-slot identity, separate freshness and coordinated editable-file publication; storage layout was split with low confidence between semantic companions and fixed ID groups. Fixed paths were recommended because semantic paths need a pointer or lookup mechanism; existing inspection can supply readable labels. The architecture agent withdrew semantic-path indirection and the identity agent withdrew an additional module ID after that concrete comparison. Annotation ergonomics were the material uncertainty at this stage; the subsequent user rejection resolves that preference in favor of clean source.

Only this proposal, its consultation records and this decision entry are added. Existing accepted requirements/contracts and the BGI execution plan remain in force; no parser, generator, runtime, generated app output, commit, merge or file-tree checkpoint changes are made.

## 2026-10-14 — keep generated persistence IDs outside Can source (accepted constraint; mechanism proposed)

The user explicitly rejects generated IDs cluttering `.can`. Preserve existing source syntax without generated identity annotations, magic comments or mandatory author names for inline prompts. This supersedes the source-carried-ID proposal and its JEV preference; the actual compiler never implemented that proposal.

Revise the same [persistence proposal](../design/proposals/build-generation/persistence-redesign.md) to keep random durable IDs and bindings in existing per-unit `unit.json` records. Retain qualified semantic selectors and minimal certificates for uniquely anchored unchanged local intervals; occurrence may select within an exactly unchanged interval, never slide across relevant insertions or serve as identity. This removes dependence on whole-file SHA/span for duplicate anonymous nodes. Formatting/comments and edits outside the interval preserve bindings. Ambiguous changed regions retain all output and require a deliberate move/fork/rebind without AI. Authoring tools can update sidecars during an already-requested edit; no mandatory editor, Git history, automatic generation or additional human approval is implied. Copies receive independent groups; moves retain IDs/code after destination checks. Ordinary Git merges are followed by deterministic binding/contract validation.

Two focused agent investigations and one cross-comparison distinguish the alternatives: per-unit certificates reuse the existing carrier and keep merge conflicts local; a sole-authority per-source baseline map can automate more local edits but adds representation and reconciliation. Choose per-unit records for the finite unchanged-region/explicit-reconciliation scope. The certificate boundary/schema needs implementation qualification; excessive real editing friction may justify the alternative, not an unlimited automatic-matching requirement. Exact identical-text swaps cannot communicate hidden ownership intent.

Three independently worded equivalent JEV Choice requests fix clean source as nonnegotiable and rotate the same balanced alternatives. [Saved requests/results](../design/jev/persistence-redesign-20261014/clean-source/1.json) and companion 2/3 records retain all uncertainty. `jev-1.13.0` selects per-unit records in all three, probabilities .84/.94/.90 and confidence .80/.92/.87, using 4,415 total tokens. This advice supports the bounded mechanism, not a reliability proof. Earlier allocator/binding observations and unaffected snapshot/deletion/binary restoration findings are reused without rerunning tests. Only design/consultation records change; no compiler, generated output, merge, commit or file-tree checkpoint change.


## 2026-10-14 — implement clean-source generated persistence (accepted)

Implement the user-authorized revision in the existing `unit.json` carrier. New IDs use 128 OS-random bits (`g-` plus 32 hex digits); keep existing IDs. Optional semantic containment selectors and normalized local-region certificates retain bindings through formatting and unrelated edits. Whole owning-source scope, one-to-one claims and unresolved displaced candidates are checked before treating anything as new. Changed ambiguous intervals require deliberate correspondence; they never authorize generation or overwrite. No generated identity is added to `.can`.

Native compile/check and saved emission consume frozen source/output inputs under cooperating leases, with root-qualified staging. Missing inline CSS now diagnoses, including pending first-generation metadata. Both bind interfaces use journaled publication: existing IDs retain current implementation; JSON `copy_from` with `unit:new` copies all current files and truthful provenance to a fresh group without AI. Reject occupied slots, stale sources and incompatible target/signature changes. Select `--generation-root` explicitly when moving sources beneath the owning app root; cross-root transfer carries the saved group deliberately and does not borrow another root's files.

Journal v2 supports exact additions, replacements and deletions, reads v1 recovery records, preserves binary bytes and refuses unexpected edits/membership. Git rollback uses complete-group replacement. Generation/refinement remain scoped patches: their current submissions do not claim complete helper/declaration/asset membership. Expanding that contract is separately proposed, not a prerequisite for preserving current code. Raw ambiguous copies/moves still require explicit rebind/fork; exact identical-text swaps cannot reveal hidden intent.

The [current BGI execution record](../design/proposals/build-generation/implementation-plan.md#current-execution--clean-source-persistence-2026-10-14) retains the finite verification, including native/host checks, the owning build and a real eight-group saved fixture clone compiled and built with the generation executable unavailable. Its 23 tracked files stayed unchanged.

The subsequent user-requested independent review closes concrete ownership, snapshot and publication gaps before commit: same-kind displaced groups require explicit reconciliation even after owner renames; legacy adoption needs a unique source claim; source-path aliases are frozen before analysis; unreadable/nonregular saved membership and malformed metadata/status fail closed; rollback validation handles both file/directory transitions without losing binary bytes or sibling helpers. The execution record records the final affected checks and reuses unchanged results. The user authorized committing this persistence scope; no merge or file-tree checkpoint advance is involved.

## 2026-10-14 — reliable Can source before model fine-tuning

**Accepted user constraint:** a specialized `.can` authoring model must fit a
12 GB GPU for inference; training may run elsewhere. Record this in REQUIREMENTS.
Model choice, inference context and measured memory remain open. This does not
change the compiler/runtime resource requirements or certify training readiness.

**Accepted correctness repairs:** follow the existing description grammar.
Formatting preserves literal `#` prose whitespace, including spaces/tabs at line
ends; ordinary `##` comments retain whitespace cleanup. Joined description CST
leaves consume intervening comment entries once, preventing a parser panic and
overlapping coverage for legal multiline descriptions. The formatter corpus
check visits the discovered corpus instead of stopping at an obsolete fixed
file count. Stored-field expression boundaries accept named traits after numeric
values, fixing the unchanged CanPromptLab `max=100 key_text_budget` source;
ordinary expressions and parameters retain spaced-unit rejection. A trait named
`m` is not globally reserved: a field's numeric value plus trait is not a duration
literal. Normative grammar text now separates the supported Rust compiler
from historical Python-prototype limitations; syntax support does not imply
semantic, emission or runtime qualification. These repairs enforce existing
contracts, rather than introducing new language semantics.

Verification: the two initial formatter regressions reproduced content loss;
their multiline case also exposed the parser panic. Final affected results are
61 syntax checks and 23 formatter checks passing, reusing unchanged passes and
rerunning the repaired corpus scope (57 formatter inputs). Source files were not
reformatted in place. Existing native `can check` with the explicit current
Values catalog reports complete, zero-diagnostic, zero-omitted results for
TeamTasks and ExpenseFlow. Rust formatting and changed-file whitespace checks
pass. These results establish their stated parser/formatter/analysis scopes,
not executable application or training-dataset acceptance.

An additional BGI-01 run passes 14/15 checks. Its existing
`negative_parse_diagnostics` fails because a prompted view containing
`card "Nope"` / `text row.title` parses successfully. HEAD already admits
`card`, `text` and `content`; BUILD_GENERATION_REQUIREMENTS and the negative
control still restrict children to canonical controls. This is an unresolved
source-contract discrepancy: reconcile those exact children with the BGI owner
before accepting either spelling as training truth. No generated-view behavior
or test expectation is changed here, and no whole-suite pass is claimed.

**Proposed training-readiness gate:** select a versioned positive source set with
its actual imports and saved generated contributions, checked against the same
compiler/catalog revision with complete diagnostics and no errors or omissions.
Preserve inline success and expected-rejection examples. For programs advertised
as executable, require compilation and their claimed behavior checks; successful
parsing alone is insufficient. Keep intentionally invalid source for explicitly
labelled repair/rejection examples, and keep historical snapshots and handwritten
desired-output witnesses out of the positive whole-program set. Separate held-out
application requirements from training examples before generating variants.

Existing DFE-01 owns source corrections, DFE-02 owns selected import-closure
integration, and BGI owns saved-generation inputs; their recorded accepted scopes
stay closed. This proposed gate adds no duplicate execution plan and does not
relax their remaining application/runtime requirements. The current repository
is not an approved training dataset. No model training, commit, merge or complete
file-tree checkpoint advancement is performed by this pass.

## 2026-10-14 — reconcile generated views and checked presentation consumers

**Accepted generated-view contract:** the earlier action-owner decision already
requires complete source-owned cards as opaque renderer bindings. Retain the
existing finite direct children: canonical cards and controls, `text`, `content`,
`history` and `require`. A card keeps its ordinary checked UI descendants and
local guards. Priority actions still need a real owning region; a generated view
does not itself supply one. Slots, nested `show`, arbitrary props, caller capture
and cross-package view export remain excluded. The row evaluates once, the
whole-view guard runs before rendering, and admitted children render in source
order. Repeated source kinds receive numeric binding suffixes; an action button
keeps `button` even though its canonical implementation is a protected form.
The generator instructions, build-generation requirements, implementation
contract and examples now use this same rule. This resolves the preceding
controls-only discrepancy; it grants no new runtime authority or unsupported
emission profile.

Three independently worded equivalent JEV Choice requests compare retaining
that finite set, restricting direct presentation to opaque cards, and admitting
all ordinary UI roots, with the accepted opaque-card rule fixed. The
[saved requests and responses](../design/jev/generated-view-contract-20261014/1.json)
and companion 2/3 records all select the finite existing set (probabilities
.99/1/.99; confidence .98/1/.98; `jev-1.13.0`, 2,463 total tokens). There is no
disagreement. These judgments advise the bounded design; compiler/runtime
checks establish its behavior.

**Accepted repairs:** generated-view lowering now records direct action buttons
under their source binding and retains nested button operation metadata inside
their opaque card. Public saved-view validation refuses relevant lowering errors
even when lowering also returns a view, closing its false acceptance of a direct
priority action without an owner. Disclosure `open` requires a nonnullable Boolean
during analysis, with the operand span and no extra error for an unresolved name.
Reference documentation consumes checked inherited `app_default_locale`, preserving
source-language identity and the existing selected-module policy. The main grammar
now includes already implemented reusable views, `show` and styles; the compiler
README distinguishes supported original-query-row history from its unsupported
argument/options/provenance profiles.

Verification: BGI-01 **16/16**, BGI-09/10 **31/31**, documentation **31/31** and UI
adapter **13/13** pass. Public BGI-11 validation subsequently passes **35/35**,
including invalid-owner refusal and a valid gated opaque card. The owning
Cloudflare build and its dependency closure pass; its existing mixed-generation
prompt check passes **1/1**, and the generated-view UI runtime suite passes
**14/14**. These checks include native compiler output joined to installed UI
factories; they do not certify every draft or approve a training corpus.

The actual `PromptStudio.can` source checks without diagnostics and compiles into
three modules with the current catalog and saved contributions. Correct four
CanPromptLab uniqueness expectations from nonexistent `error(unique)` to the
canonical `error(conflict)`, matching both builtin and generated State key
failures. Its subsequent complete check has no example-error diagnostic. The
remaining five missing-contribution errors and dependent field errors are held
by its 20 legacy handwritten saved records: their old metadata has no accepted
current binding. Existing draft witnesses remain desired-output evidence, not
an executable positive training example. BGI owns explicit compatible adoption
and saved contributions; the source correction does not claim that release.

## 2026-10-14 — format computed anonymous messages with their checked schemas

**Accepted:** explicit `format` consumes anonymous descriptors selected through
the checked builtin `choose`, including nested/grouped choices and immutable
aliases. Retain every reachable checked leaf and validate all source/translation
placeholders, even for an unselected branch. Raw leaves have an empty schema;
bound leaves retain their inferred parameter types. Different placeholder names
and types are supported. Condition and both operands keep their eager, once-only
authored evaluation; the surrounding locale argument retains its source position.
Only the selected descriptor's already captured values are formatted.

The existing runtime descriptor already carries canonical source locale and
typed parameter entries. Emit a finite list of checked formatter schemas, match
that descriptor's exact own parameter names/types and canonical locale, and apply
the corresponding Values presentation mapping. Reuse the existing locale
normalizer. Equivalent observable schemas may coalesce; conflicting presentation
mappings refuse. The existing signature integrity checks also reject foreign,
inherited or accessor parameter metadata before conversion. This uses compiler
analysis/IR metadata and the existing descriptor; it adds no public syntax,
runtime carrier or dependency. It does not admit arbitrary descriptor-producing
functions, indexing, coalescing, nullable descriptors or every UI/outbound sink.

The initial actual CLI check reproduced E3005 for
`format(choose(true,"Hi"@{},"Bye"@{}),locale=null)`. Three independently worded
equivalent JEV Choice requests compare empty-schema-only choices, one shared
schema and finite alternatives using existing descriptor metadata. The
[saved requests/results](../design/jev/computed-message-format-20261014/1.json)
and companion 2/3 records all select finite alternatives (probability/confidence
1 in each; `jev-1.13.0`, 3,807 total tokens). There is no disagreement. The bounded
source graph and exact schema matching remain implementation obligations, not
facts proved by the judgments.

Five anonymous-message coverage checks pass, including actual installed-runtime
results for both selections, differing names/types, equal schemas with opposite
capture order, nested choices, aliases, canonical source locale, authored
locale-first order and first-failure identity. Invalid reachable placeholders
and mixed/nullable operands refuse without artifacts. Four existing localized
formatter checks, six slot-coverage checks and eleven decision-source checks
also pass. These results close this explicit formatter scope while preserving
the broader S9-Q01/C17 remainder and the existing 58/67 completion count.

The compatibility checks also exposed an ordinary button-contract defect:
`button submit=true` outside a form compiled, and non-destination combinations
could carry conflicting bindings. Analysis now requires exactly one binding
and an inherited canonical form/edit/preferences owner for submit. Layout
wrappers preserve that ancestry; the separate direct priority-action owner
rules stay unchanged. Positive direct/wrapped forms compile, and edit/preferences
controls pass analysis without claiming their broader runtime profiles. Literal
`submit=true`, caption typing/purity and canonical operation admission remain
with their existing checks. Two older runtime-fixture `principal.admitted_at`
values now include mandatory wire milliseconds; accepted `datetime(...)` source
constructor syntax is unchanged.

Final affected checks pass **10/10**, covering the new button controls, both
previous binding-suite failures, the updated exact TeamTasks formatter-schema
assertion, button/catalog compatibility and the saved-view button compile join.
Reusing unchanged checks yields **137/137** codegen and **10/10** anonymous
binding checks at their affected scopes. The new formatter native tests and
other accepted results above are not repeated. No model training, complete
language/application certification, commit, merge or file-tree checkpoint
advancement is claimed.


## 2026-10-14 — adopt legacy saved outputs and enforce pure field checks

**Accepted:** explicit `can gen bind` may adopt a recognizable untouched legacy
saved group against an explicitly selected current definition and source revision.
The current source owns association and contract; the original prompt, file hashes
and handwritten/provider provenance remain historical evidence. Named labels and
kind families must agree; anonymous correspondence requires explicit selection.
Malformed modern records never fall back to legacy intake. Preserve leases,
occupied/duplicate-source refusal and journal publication. Copy legacy `server.js`
to a missing canonical `implementation.js` for executable units without deleting
or replacing the original. Automatic compile fallback remains at its prior scope.
PromptLab's three styles with no live host must be retained outside active saved
output discovery, not silently assigned to different source.

**Accepted:** a named or inline trait attached only to required native `text`
fields may supply `implementation.js` exporting `check(value)`. The existing
`contributions.can` supplies one matching typed field template; `value:text`
adds no artificial constraint when the check alone supplies behavior. The
compiler derives `state.field-validation@1`, `validate-fields`, text input,
Boolean result and empty reads/effects/authority. A separate implementation
closure fingerprint accompanies the existing contribution fingerprint. Artifacts require the existing `state.field-validation` capability at version 1,
so older installed consumers refuse instead of ignoring the additional contract.
Model traits, nullable/other field types and metadata-invented producer authority
remain refused. No additional public source syntax or dependency is needed.

State evaluates checks in checked application order over normalized, hook-adjusted
text on each create/update, before provisional publication, history and unique
claims. A trusted hook can transform input before this final-value check. Strict
`true` succeeds; `false`, non-Boolean results and exceptions produce canonical
`validation` with no committed partial state. Existing admission, work accounting,
transaction failure, replay and commit remain authoritative. Desired migration
validation checks both staged and retained rows before activation, without silently
normalizing stored data. Privileged example materialization must enforce the same
field constraints; it does not claim user CRUD authorization.

The verified saved-module loader checks exact implementation/import bytes and
passes projected text, with no record/store/permission handles. As with existing
computed keys, these are trusted adopted modules, not a JavaScript isolation
boundary or proof of arbitrary module purity. General sandboxing and additional
field types are separate proposals, not prerequisites invented for this repair.

Three independently worded JEV Choice requests compared this trait extension,
two native algorithm-specific constraints and a standalone-keyword rewrite. All
selected the trait extension with probability/confidence 1 (`jev-1.13.0`, 4,150
total tokens), with no disagreement. [Requests and responses](../design/jev/field-trait-validation-20261014/1.json)
and companion 2/3 preserve the evidence and uncertainty. These are design advice;
compiler, runtime and actual app validation remain required. Implementation and
qualification are in progress; no training or whole-language acceptance is claimed.


The main grammar now records existing named/inline traits and custom keyword
syntax. Its reconciliation exposed a parser asymmetry: adjacent named traits
worked on models but a stored field required lookahead to the final suffix.
Accept each field suffix name in authored order after native modifiers, preserving
unknown-trait resolution and label/description boundaries. This admits the same
finite checked contribution composition on both attachment kinds, including
`text min=1 max=100 clean budget`, without a new syntax.


Actual PromptLab compilation after binding exposed another ownership mismatch:
generation discovery and authored-trait compatibility used the first module in a
file, although the resolver supports a composition app followed by packages.
Discover prompts, target names, style uses and anonymous evidence separately per
owning app/package; read authored model constraints from their checked module
span. Preserve the source composition and explicitly rebind affected saved groups
to the corrected owner. Repeated local trait/style names in distinct packages do
not conflict or cross-resolve. This is a demonstrated compiler repair, not an
app-source workaround.

Contributed model fields retain static literal captions through the existing
field-label IR, AppDefinition and prepared form path. Validate those captions
with the existing empty-schema ICU checker and use the receiving module's logical
source locale. Unsupported computed, descriptor, path or translation-table
captions refuse explicitly. Field-trait constraints cannot replace an authored
caption or its translations. Additional generated translation profiles remain
proposed; silently dropping a supplied caption is not supported behavior.

Trait leaf admission must match existing native State/Values associations:
Boolean, integer, decimal, text, email, timezone, date, datetime, duration,
money, user, file and inline enums, with one array wrapper and optional outer
nullability. Existing scalar aliases remain valid. Nested arrays and the currently
unmapped url, locale, currency, member, json, bytes and secret contributions
refuse until their ordinary storage associations exist. Model contributions
continue to require explicit defaults, including `=null` and `=[]`; this repair
does not infer omitted carrier defaults. Decode defaults through the existing
exact Values codecs rather than converting integer/decimal tokens through
JavaScript Number. Nonnullable object-like defaults still require an expressible
source constant; nullable and empty-array forms do not invent one.

The same default must have the same artifact wire shape whether authored directly
or contributed: exact integer/decimal strings, duration milliseconds, Boolean/null
values, enum strings and recursively encoded arrays. Preserve decimal source scale
in compiler output, as ordinary fields do; State compares reused defaults after
the existing Values codec normalization. Preserve whitespace inside array string
literals. Native numeric bounds also use exact wire strings; length bounds retain
safe nonnegative JSON integers. Nullable decimal bounds use the underlying decimal
type rather than being parsed as integers.

Actual application qualification also requires the local preview to admit the
already supported one-app, same-file package composition. Remove the lexical
blanket refusal of `uses=` and `package`; the native compiler still resolves
references, source capture still verifies the complete file inventory, and the
preview retains its import, multiple-app, resource and capability restrictions.
Optional local actor roles resolve only against the verified compiled definition
and are granted through Identity's owner API; ordinary starts grant no extra roles.
This introduces no production role-assignment endpoint.

Source example recipes must initialize dependencies before their consumers,
including the definitions retained for otherwise unused fixtures. Fixture lookup
uses the owning module's fixture symbols rather than a flat name map that can be
overwritten by a scenario parameter. Returned-record observations retain the
actual successful result and use the existing caller-authorized projection; a
test observation is not authority to read private fields. These are repairs to
the existing example contract, not changes to the authored expected outcomes.

The default-wire correspondence check also covers offset/no-millisecond datetime
source literals: contributed and directly authored fields both emit the existing
canonical UTC millisecond wire representation. Its focused native check passes;
the five example-binding checks invalidated by a concurrent catalog cache refresh
pass after serializing that refresh, restoring all eight checks at their original
scope. Package build/catalog output must remain fixed during consumers' captures.

Actual PromptLab execution then exposed the remaining generated CRUD candidate
admission gap: all 26 original rows stopped during registry setup because `when`
callbacks were not connected to canonical admission. The accepted semantics in
DESIGN.md remain unchanged: normalize the proposed create/update row, evaluate
`when` before staging, and use the existing row for delete. Candidate field reads
see the proposed row; scans see the provisional store before this write, including
earlier effects. Ordinary scenario create/set effects must not inherit the CRUD
guard. Their own guards, permissions, locks and final invariants remain in force.

**Accepted implementation choice; qualification in progress:** bind the existing
verified generated CRUD callback to an internal owner-scoped stage option at that
boundary. Check its exact operation/module/model/key association before admitting
the manifest's `when` marker. Reuse native actor, parent and bounded query adapters,
the provisional reader, work budget and failure latch. A false predicate refuses
with `rule_failed`; malformed results/errors must fail closed. Do not replace the
callback with an unguarded manifest, change source policy or introduce a parallel
predicate language. The existing restricted invariant adapter alone does not
establish query support; faithful pre-write queries remain an implementation and
validation obligation.

Three equivalent independently worded JEV Choice requests compared this callback
bridge with a complete serializable predicate AST/interpreter and an explicitly
limited data-predicate subset. All chose the bridge with probability/confidence 1
(`jev-1.13.0`, 4,265 tokens), with no disagreement. [Saved requests and responses](../design/jev/crud-candidate-admission-20261014/1.json)
and companion 2/3 retain the alternatives and uncertainty. This is advice, not
runtime proof. Four additional source rows independently specify catalog key
scope and the `É`/`é` distinction; the current app has 30 rows awaiting successful
runtime qualification. Browser retry uses an isolated temporary preview namespace
so the unrelated active ActionGallery session remains owned by its original caller.

PromptLab's source also misused unconditional field locks as CRUD field lists.
Such locks prohibit scenario changes and row removal as well (DESIGN.md318), so
they made the required archive/restore and note-removal workflows impossible.
Remove those three locks: the existing CRUD allowlists already exclude archive
evidence and server-owned Note.author, while the attributed archive scenarios and
stored invariants retain their declared authority. Do not weaken lock semantics
in the runtime. Archived fixture rows now supply consistent actor/time evidence;
expected archive attribution names the selected `editor` fixture, not the distinct
test `self` account. The revised 30-row source compiles without diagnostics.

The installed example materializer has a distinct unfinished gap: parent models
and computed-key fixture overrides refuse, and its computed-key seed branch
incorrectly tries user CRUD as `self`. DESIGN.md544 requires privileged stored
snapshots with complete constraint/reference/invariant/unique validation, no
CRUD guards/hooks/events and no claimed historical workflow. It may initialize
server-owned domain fields. This cannot be repaired by granting `self` production
roles or bypassing stored-data checks. Actual source-example qualification remains
open until that snapshot path is implemented and executed.

**Accepted implementation choice; qualification in progress:** add an internal
fixture stage cause only for a test owner context, with no production source or
request switch. Reuse the same model table, codecs, field checks, containment,
references, final invariants and net unique claims. Setup may initialize declared
server-owned domain fields; it does not run CRUD admission/hooks, pre-state locks
or business history/events. Apply the entire override batch before final validation
and preserve initial version/time/attribution. Do not mix setup with operation
stages. The installed adapter opens a separately checked native policy frame from
the actual test context, commits once under the revision fence and closes it on
every exit. It does not manufacture an admitted operation or grant roles. Existing
file/provider fixture profiles remain explicitly unsupported.

Three equivalent independently worded JEV Choice requests compare this owner
snapshot path with a complete shadow-store rebuild/claim translation and a
migration-validation adapter. All choose the owner path with confidence/probability
1 (`jev-1.13.0`, 4,562 tokens). [Requests and responses](../design/jev/fixture-snapshot-admission-20261014/1.json)
and companion 2/3 preserve the alternatives and remaining implementation risks.
No disagreement occurred; validation still owns acceptance. User recipes resolve
to the actual provisioned Identity references, and one row clock must feed fixture
expressions, the real operation and its observations.

The native CRUD consumer also exposed lexical query capture: lowering
`stored.name == row.name` inside a CRUD predicate renamed `stored` to `row`, making
both sides read the query row. Preserve the outer candidate binding during query
parameter normalization; do not rewrite the source example to hide the defect.
The established native query correspondence checks retain their exact ownership
and must continue to pass after this repair.

The native CRUD consumer now passes with the original query preserved. Compiler
checks cover the candidate binding, a nested outer query binding and a locally
bound `row`; ordinary predicates retain their existing canonical spelling. The
fixture snapshot owner passes four affected checks, and all eight installed
example-runner checks pass after replacing two obsolete setup-version assertions
with the specified initial version/time/attribution behavior. The package build
and catalog refresh pass. These bounded results do not qualify PromptLab itself.

Actual PromptLab setup exposes a further compiler omission: the native local-rule
classifier rejects its nullable archive-evidence presence checks, omitting the
whole model-policy contract. Admit checked equality/inequality with null for
direct owning nullable user/datetime fields through the existing policy path.
Retain the exact source fields/types and existing runtime invariant evaluator;
this adds no reference traversal, arithmetic, context or query authority. Native
emission and valid/invalid archive-evidence invocation own acceptance. The source
rules and expected outcomes stay unchanged. The 12 profile and seven producer
checks pass: incomplete archive evidence rejects without row/history changes,
the authored archive scenario commits actor/time evidence, and the original
PromptLab emits both Entry and Tag policies with their exact owning bindings.

The same existing example contract requires `self`, `other` and `outsider` to be
the provisioned row's typed user references. Test factories currently capture
placeholder strings before provisioning. Resolve these built-in references from
the row binding object when fixture/input/expected/observation closures execute,
as already done for `now`; preserve lexical shadowing and load-time caller
selection. The runner may recognize only identities it provisioned in that row.
Do not reload every suite per row, invent grants or convert arbitrary strings to
users. A native source example with an explicit `server` domain value of `other`
and a real invocation as `self` owns this finite compiler/runtime acceptance.
The nine compiler BDD runtime checks and affected ExpenseFlow emission golden
pass, including stale-factory/live-row and lexical-shadowing controls. Installed
row identity now passes its four native source rows, and the complete installed
runner suite passes nine checks. PromptLab reaches 13 passing rows; the other 17
expose a compiler fixture-dependency defect: a module-wide discovery union was
reused as the current table's seeded baseline, so one row's `editor` reference
suppressed that fixture in later rows. Keep the actual common/seed dependency
closure separate from module discovery and each row's closure. The runtime must
continue to materialize only that row's required fixtures; auto-seeding every
declared fixture would change collection and uniqueness outcomes. Original rows
remain unchanged and own the application retry.
The focused emitted/Testkit regression passes with repeated `editor` references
in caller, field-cell, expected and observation positions. A separate Bob-seeded
table verifies that neither fixture leaks into the other's rows. Fresh PromptLab
output retains `editor` in all 24 applicable row dependency lists.

The subsequent actual PromptLab run passes 29/30 rows with no setup failures or
unsupported rows. Its sole failure is the existing independent-Catalog case:
the same canonical Entry code incorrectly conflicts across distinct parents.
DESIGN.md131 and the keyword contract already require the owning parent/team/app
scope; repair the owning implementation rather than broaden uniqueness or alter
the example. Browser qualification separately reaches its isolated session but
stops at preview construction (`preview_build_failed`) before UI actions. Both
remaining failures are concrete implementation work; training remains gated.

**Accepted parent-key repair and installed-state boundary:** reuse the existing
canonical parent-scope wrapper for computed claim/release values in mutation,
installation, migration validation and all changed/retained/dropped-row migration
paths. Root/team key bytes and the pure `canonicalKey(text)` ABI remain unchanged.
The source schema itself already declares containment. An `oldModels` table with
containment removed would fabricate predecessor source semantics and is not a
valid repair description for old raw claims.

Add a narrow optional trusted-owner storage read, `uniqueOwner(model,keyName,keyValue)`,
to the real memory/D1/DO owners. Contained computed mutations require this read
and reject relevant legacy raw claims before staging; root/team profiles retain
their existing behavior. Classify claim ownership using the actual stored row,
pure output and canonical scoped value, including raw/scoped string overlaps.
Missing support or inconsistent ownership fails closed. Reuse the owner work
budget and revision fence; no source or request endpoint gains this read.

An explicit derived-index repair through the trusted State owner must validate a
complete bounded affected row set and final collisions, then release old claims
and publish canonical claims atomically under the existing fence. It changes no
record data, versions, history, permissions or source-schema provenance. Ordinary
writes do not silently migrate installed indexes. Fresh, valid legacy, mixed
encoding, failed-repair and post-repair behavior own acceptance; no existing store
is claimed repaired merely because its runtime code was replaced.

The first three JEV requests split two for bounded refusal and one for a persisted
version, at low confidence (0.37–0.46). Inspection corrected two assumptions: the
storage port has no claim read, and existing activation's predecessor table is a
source schema rather than a physical-index profile. Three corrected equivalent
requests compare adding the read plus explicit repair, adding a persisted version
plus repair, and rebuilding the index on every write. Two favor lookup/repair
(confidence 0.51/0.56); one favors rebuilding (0.30). [All requests and responses](../design/jev/computed-key-parent-scope-20261014/1.json)
and the `corrected/` directory retain the disagreement and correction (9,296 tokens,
`jev-1.13.0`). The choice rests on the actual interfaces and preserving indexed
write costs: a complete rebuild on every mutation would broaden work/refusal
behavior, while a persisted version crosses more installation/admission state.
Advice remains uncertain; the direct owner and repair checks determine acceptance.

The preview failure is independently an Identity grammar mismatch: its role
validator excludes underscores permitted by Can `NAME`. Match both qualified
segments to `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, keep `owner` and the two-segment shape, and
reject trailing line terminators. Verify actual owner-managed grants, revocation,
invitation acceptance/ceilings and unauthorized callers; do not bypass Identity
to seed preview actors. Surfacing a safe actionable preview-build error remains
a separate diagnostic proposal.

The parent-scope change passes all 31 affected State checks: the final retry
corrects only the version expectation for an explicit source backfill, which
increments that row once. Physical index repair separately proves unchanged
rows, versions and history. Five real Memory/D1/Durable Object storage checks
pass, as do both Identity role grammar/authority checks and the 24-package build.
The trusted claim read is forwarded through installed staged/join/producer store
wrappers without exposing it to source-facing policy or request objects.

The explicit repair covers valid legacy indexes under the current pure key
binding, including mixed raw/scoped overlap. A lookup-only port cannot discover
arbitrary orphan claims or claims from an unknown historical key algorithm;
corrupt-index reconstruction is outside this accepted repair scope. No installed
store has been repaired by these tests. Actual PromptLab source and browser
qualification now consume the rebuilt runtime and retain their separate gates.

**2026-10-15 actual application result:** all 30 original/current PromptLab source
rows pass through the installed canonical runtime, with zero setup failures or
unsupported rows. This closes the independent-Catalog failure without changing
its expected outcome. Reuse that result for the unchanged source-row scope.
Isolated rows do not prove key availability after a failed operation or receipt
replay across calls; the required actual-app permission/rollback/replay sequence
remains a separate finite check. Browser retry gets past Identity seeding and
fails at the installed authenticated page probe with HTTP 400, before any UI
actions. That concrete runtime failure, archive-evidence assertions, and the
remaining documented browser states/baselines retain their own acceptance.

The actual-app native sequence passes member CRUD/foreign-note refusals and
failed-write key preservation/reuse before failing at successful scenario replay.
The runtime refusal is correct: `add_entry` has no compiler-emitted result
disclosure, so its first invocation cannot issue a genuine saved association.
The checked Create producer currently excludes named source roles and models with
trait-contributed fields. Extend their existing checked role and Given-field
provenance correspondence for the actual source; keep unassociated legacy replay
refused. No new receipt authority may be inferred from the returned value alone.

**Accepted installed page binding; qualification in progress:** the compiler
already emits stable collection occurrences. Installed worker construction omits
the required trusted page binding. Extend the existing optional static
`pageReads` seam with a host-owned factory, resolved once after the current
Identity owner boundary selects the physical store. Validate the returned app
and owner against that selected context, and retain it for the request's read
scope. Static bindings preserve their existing checks. The worker derives the
factory from its verified declared app/configured owner routes and existing exact
source identity. Reuse the existing private form key with the page cursor codec's
separate MAC domain; add no URL/source authority or new secret configuration.
Cursor occurrence/query/actor/team/source checks, original query time, expiry and
final State authority/revision checks remain unchanged.

Three equivalent independently worded JEV Choice requests compared this factory
with an explicit trusted owner-binding map and separate owner-specific assemblies.
All selected the factory (confidence 0.91/0.92/0.85; selected probability
0.94/0.95/0.90; `jev-1.13.0`, 3,617 tokens). [Saved requests and responses](../design/jev/page-owner-binding-20261015/1.json)
and companion 2/3 retain all alternatives and uncertainty. No disagreement needs
resolution. This avoids duplicate route configuration and assembly lifecycle
changes; direct installed host/owner/cursor checks still own acceptance.

Archive presentation also exposes a demonstrated adapter mismatch: canonical
`text` forwards native UserRef/DatetimeValue objects to a formatter that expects
typed scalar operands. DESIGN's existing stable user identity rule and the
existing exact datetime formatter define the result. Admit those native shapes
at the text boundary, escape/isolate the stable user ID and route datetime through
the existing Values-backed formatter. Preserve null behavior and refuse malformed
or arbitrary objects without stringification/accessor evaluation. This adds no
directory lookup, new source type or timezone policy. Browser assertions compare
visible archive evidence with the actual canonical changed-row projection, then
verify its removal after restoration; prepared assertions alone are not acceptance.

The compiler's focused library-test build exposed a stale test already present on
HEAD: it calls the removed `synthesize_inline_unit` helper and expects silent
empty-style synthesis. Remove that obsolete test, not restore the superseded
behavior. The existing BGI02 missing-primary refusal check owns the accepted
requirement and its unchanged passing result is reused. Production intake behavior
is unchanged by this test cleanup.

Native user/datetime presentation passes all 101 affected UI component/leaf checks,
including visible text, plain accessible names, exact temporal decoding and
malformed-object refusal. One shared internal adapter keeps visible and accessible
sinks consistent while each sink retains its own escaping. The installed page
binding also preserves the old static-mismatch order: refuse before selecting or
initializing a physical owner store. Only the new trusted factory resolves after
selection. Its actual host regression includes a 25+1 page continuation,
cross-owner cursor refusal and static mismatch with no selection; execution is

That host regression and the focused installed worker configuration check now

[query/reference consultations](../design/jev/boolean-read-query-closure-20261015/1.json)
and companions 2/3 selected this existing-observation extension (probability
1/.97/.99, confidence 1/.95/.98). This dependency is necessary for the original

the directory.

when the corresponding implementation and original-source checks pass. Broader

User-mail implementation acceptance: Contracts/Services/State/Work/Cloudflare emits pass; thirteen contract checks, seven affected Work registry/pin checks and the eight-check target universe pass at their retained scopes. The new durable recipient component and existing ordinary-mail component pass.
